identity.name: yexca
identity.tagline: I build local-first tools, agent workflows, and knowledge systems.
identity.description: A Master's student exploring how AI, agents, and local software can become dependable personal systems. Most of my work starts with a small, recurring friction: preparing data, running models locally, organizing media, or keeping notes usable across four languages. This blog is where I write those down, along with what I'm thinking about life.

items.title: Agents and the harness around them
items.text: A fully local assistant on ZeroClaw, Ollama and Matrix, tools wired in through an MCP gateway, and a lot of building with Codex and Claude Code.

items.title: Local AI pipelines
items.text: ComfyUI image workflows, audio prep for AI covers, YOLO experiments, and models that run on my own machines.

items.title: A self-hosted home stack
items.text: Small services on my NAS for voice works, music, RSS, and images, plus a start page that ties them together.

items.title: Local-first
items.text: Keep data, models, and control close when that makes the system clearer and more dependable.

items.title: Inspectable
items.text: Make inputs, state, and failures visible enough to debug and improve.

items.title: Composable
items.text: Connect models, tools, storage, and human decisions into one workflow.

items.title: Worth maintaining
items.text: Prefer small systems that stay useful after the first experiment.

timeline.title: The story of this site
timeline.today: And then there is today. The story keeps going.

items.label: WordPress
items.title: A place to write things down
items.body: The blog began as a small place for learning notes, fixes, and experiments I did not want to lose. A place to create freely? Sounds cool, doesn't it? ＼(~o~)／

items.label: Astra
items.title: The first version went live
items.body: Several days and a couple of resets later, the Astra theme finally made it look decent.

items.label: Sakurairo
items.title: Learning by changing themes
items.body: Early theme changes were not just decoration. They were how I learned what kind of site felt like mine. Adorable, isn't it?

items.label: Argon
items.title: A blog that could stay around
items.body: Argon was pretty and practical enough for long-term writing, problem solving, and daily maintenance.

items.label: Docker
items.title: Deployment became reproducible
items.body: Moving everything to Docker turned server setup from memory work into infrastructure notes I could repeat.

items.label: Jekyll
items.title: Toward static generation
items.body: Jekyll was lighter and geekier, and moved the blog from a themed website toward a static publishing workflow.

items.label: Hugo
items.title: A multilingual knowledge base
items.body: Hugo brought internationalization, a translation workflow, and a structure that suits notes across languages. ( •̀ ω •́ )✧

items.label: Counter
items.title: A small sign of life
items.body: A cute visitor counter makes the page feel visited and alive.

items.label: Stack
items.title: Introducing the blog again
items.body: Refactoring the Stack theme became a chance to rethink what this blog records now: code, tools, notes, and life.

items.label: Redesign
items.title: Quieter pages
items.body: Archives, links, and this page were redesigned: less decoration, more to read.

footer: Life is an adventure game, with a new map and new quests every day. Stay curious, and keep exploring!
